Lighter and Lighter on Robinhood Chain expose the
same REST API, WebSocket API and transaction format
. Pick the base URL and chain ID that match the exchange you are integrating; the server selector in each endpoint's
Test it
panel lists all four.

WebSocket

Endpoints marked
Lighter on Robinhood Chain only
(points, referral points) exist only on the RH servers. Endpoints marked
Lighter only
(binary options) exist only on the Lighter servers.
Lighter RH is a
separate exchange
: accounts, balances, API keys, nonces and account indexes don't carry over, and mainnet signatures use distinct chain IDs. The two testnets both use chain ID
300
; keep the base URL and chain ID together instead of relying on chain ID alone to distinguish testnets. See
Lighter on Robinhood Chain
.
Sections
REST API
– almost every endpoint is under
/api/v1/
, grouped by resource. Status (
/
) and info (
/info
) are root endpoints.
WebSocket
– streaming market and account data, and sending transactions over WebSocket.
Explorer API
– blocks, batches, search, statistics, logs by hash, account logs/assets/positions and market logs. The base URLs are
https://explorer.elliot.ai/api
(Lighter) and
https://explorerapi.rh.lighter.xyz/api
(Robinhood Chain).

On this page
Lighter only.
Get events and registered order books, including scheduled events with no books. event_ids and market_ids accept up to 50 comma-separated positive IDs, are mutually exclusive, and use the same filters, sorting and pagination. market_ids returns each related event once with all its order books. Defaults to descending id. start_at sorting uses (start_at, event_id); cursor identifies an existing event and excludes it in the requested direction. tag filters across creators; creator_account_index is an optional additional filter. active=true requires a tradeable outcome; active=false includes scheduled and closed events.
Use this endpoint to discover binary options markets and read their actual trading windows, decimals and market fees. Binary options are excluded from
orderBookDetails
. See
Discover markets
for examples, pagination and lifecycle statuses.

Get fee tiers. filter=perps|spot returns the regular user tiers (both market types share them). filter=bo returns BO volume tiers and LIT staking discount tiers; filter=all returns everything. On this page
Lighter only.
Get binary-options realized PnL for an authenticated account, grouped by event and ordered newest event first. cursor is an exclusive event id; event_id returns a single event. Every outcome the account has traded is reported, including markets still open or unsettled, so an entry never disappears as the account trades. Per outcome, total_pnl is all realized PnL so far including settlement, and settlement_pnl is null until the market settles with a position to settle, then the string 0.000000 for an actual zero-PnL settlement. An event's total_pnl is the sum of its listed outcomes. Missing display metadata uses zero/empty values.
total_pnl
is realized PnL
gross of fees
, including settlement. Subtract trading fees separately when calculating net PnL.
settlement_pnl
is
null
until the market settles with a position to settle; a settled zero-PnL position returns
"0.000000"
. Supply an account auth token in the
authorization
header. See
Positions and settlement
for payout semantics and an example.

Get the OHLC candles (1s = the exact price observations, or 30s) of an up/down market series (symbol + duration, e.g. btc/5m) in a bounded time range (at most 24h), oldest first. Pass next_cursor as start_timestamp to page forward; live candles are on the up_down_candle/// websocket channel.

Response Description:
1)
Taker and maker fees
are in percentage.
2)
Min base amount:
The amount of base token that can be traded in a single order.
3)
Min quote amount:
The amount of quote token that can be traded in a single order.
4)
Supported size decimals:
The number of decimal places that can be used for the size of the order.
5)
Supported price decimals:
The number of decimal places that can be used for the price of the order.
6)
Supported quote decimals:
Size Decimals + Quote Decimals.
For perpetual markets, open_interest_usd is double-sided open interest (longs + shorts) in USDC at the mark price, and open_interest_limit is the double-sided cap in base tokens at the current mark price. The legacy open_interest field should not be used to derive perpetual open interest; use orderBookDetails.open_interest or open_interest_usd instead.

https://docs.lighter.xyz/api/websocket.title: WebSocket
https://docs.lighter.xyz/api/websocket.content:
For the complete documentation index, see
llms.txt
. This page is also available as
Markdown
.
This page will help you get started with the Lighter WebSocket server.
Connection
Environment
URL
Lighter mainnet
wss://mainnet.zklighter.elliot.ai/stream
Lighter testnet
wss://testnet.zklighter.elliot.ai/stream
Robinhood Chain mainnet
wss://api.rh.lighter.xyz/stream
Robinhood Chain testnet
wss://api.rh-testnet.lighter.xyz/stream
You can directly connect to the WebSocket server using wscat:
GitBook Assistant
Ask
Copy
wscat
-c
'
wss://mainnet.zklighter.elliot.ai/stream
'
If you're connecting from a restricted region, you can still access read-only data:
GitBook Assistant
Ask
Copy
wscat
-c
'
wss://mainnet.zklighter.elliot.ai/stream?readonly=true
'
Message envelope
Message
Meaning
type: "connected"
The socket is connected; subscribe to the channels you need.
type: "subscribed/<channel>"
Subscription acknowledgement with the initial snapshot.
type: "update/<channel>"
A subsequent update. Apply it according to that channel's rules.
error: {code, message}
Request or subscription failed. Errors need not contain a
type
field; an optional
id
identifies the request.
Subscribe requests use slash-separated channel names; response
channel
values use colons. Private channels take an
auth
token inside the subscribe message, as shown below. This WebSocket field is separate from REST authentication, which uses the
Authorization
header. Public-pool data does not require authentication; see
pool_data
and
pool_info
.
Structure blocks below use placeholders such as
INTEGER
,
STRING
and
FLOAT
; they describe payloads and are not literal JSON. Example response blocks are JSON.
transaction_time
is in microseconds and may be omitted when no transaction execution time is available. See
Timestamps
for field-specific units.
Keepalive Requirements
Clients are responsible for keeping the connection alive by sending at least one frame every
2 minutes
. This can be either:
A
WebSocket ping frame
Any application-level message
Clients sending
{"type":"ping"}
will receive back
{"type":"pong"}
.
If the server receives no frames from a client within the 2-minute window, it will close the connection.
Support for
permessage-deflate
compression is enabled.
Writes to slow clients time out after 250 ms by default. Keep reading messages continuously; if the connection closes, reconnect and resubscribe to obtain fresh snapshots.
Send Tx
You can send transactions using the websocket as follows:
GitBook Assistant
Ask
Copy
{
"type": "jsonapi/sendtx",
"data": {
"id": STRING, // returned in the ws response
"tx_type": INTEGER,
"tx_info": ...
}
}
The
tx_type
options can be found in the
SignerClient
file, while
tx_info
can be generated using the sign methods in the SignerClient.
Example:
create_modify_cancel_order_ws.py
Send Batch Tx
You can send batch transactions to execute up to 50 transactions in a single message. Larger batches are rejected with error
21514
.
GitBook Assistant
Ask
Copy
{
"type": "jsonapi/sendtxbatch",
"data": {
"id": STRING, // returned in the ws response
"tx_types": "[INTEGER]",
"tx_infos": "[tx_info]"
}
}
The
tx_type
options can be found in the
SignerClient
file, while
tx_info
can be generated using the sign methods in the SignerClient.
Example:
ws_send_batch_tx.py
Types
These types are shared across channels. Fields marked optional are omitted when zero or empty. Field names and numeric/string representations match the API.
Transaction JSON
To decode
event_info
, you can refer to
Data Structures
.
GitBook Assistant
Ask
Copy
Transaction = {
"hash": STRING,
"type": INTEGER,
"info": STRING,                // json object as string, attributes depending on the tx type
"event_info": STRING,          // json object as string, attributes depending on the tx type

Order Book
The order book channel sends the new ask and bid orders for the given market in batches, every 50ms. While the nonce is tied to Lighter's matching engine, the offset is tied to the API servers; hence, you can expect the offset to change drastically on reconnection if you're routed to a different server. Regardless, on each update the offset will increase, but it's not guaranteed to be continuous. Additionally, this channel sends a complete snapshot on subscription, but only state changes after that. To verify the continuity of the data, you can check that
begin_nonce
on the current update matches the
nonce
(i.e.
last_nonce
) of the previous update.
GitBook Assistant
Ask
Copy
{
"type": "subscribe",
"channel": "order_book/{MARKET_INDEX}"
}
